around.headline: Bengaluru man duped of ₹26 lakh with promise of a government job; separate case sees fake DRDO officer swindle woman of ₹2.3 lakh
around.summary: Police are probing two impersonation scams this week — a fraudster took ₹26 lakh promising a govt job with no interview, and a fake DRDO officer conned a woman out of ₹2.3 lakh. No legitimate government recruitment or scheme ever asks for upfront cash outside an official notification.

around.headline: Elderly couple die by suicide in Bengaluru; financial stress over medical expenses suspected
around.summary: Police suspect the couple, who reportedly didn't want to burden their daughters, were struggling with medical costs. If you or someone you know is in distress, the Kiran mental health helpline (1800-599-0019) is free and available 24/7.
around.source: The Hindu / The New Indian Express

around.headline: Kengeri–Hejjala railway under-bridge opens, ending a 7-month commuter ordeal in West Bengaluru
around.summary: The new under-bridge is open to traffic today, resolving months of detours and congestion on the Kengeri-Hejjala stretch. If this is on your regular route, expect a smoother, faster commute from today.

around.headline: BMTC to launch contactless 'tap card' payments, no PIN needed
around.summary: Commuters will soon be able to tap a card to pay bus fares without entering a PIN, similar to metro smart cards. Keep an eye out for rollout details if you use BMTC daily and want to skip cash or ticket queues.

around.headline: ₹5,000 fine proposed for driving or parking on Bengaluru footpaths
around.summary: Minister Krishna Byre Gowda has proposed a steep fine as footpath-driving cases have soared and footpath-parking cases have doubled citywide. If you ride a two-wheeler, avoid footpath shortcuts even in traffic — enforcement is likely to tighten soon.

around.headline: Iran's military says it attacked US bases in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait as West Asia tensions escalate
around.summary: The strikes mark a serious escalation in the region, coming as an LPG tanker with 28 Indians aboard was also attacked in Iranian waters (crew reported safe). If you have family working in the Gulf or travel plans there, watch for advisories and possible fuel-price ripple effects at home.

street_smart.title: A 'contact' says he can get you or a family member a confirmed government job — no interview, just a processing fee paid upfront. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real cases reported today: a Bengaluru man lost ₹26 lakh after being promised a government job, and separately a woman was duped of ₹2.3 lakh by a fake DRDO officer — both impersonation scams built on the promise of official access (The Times of India).
street_smart.situation: He's shown you an ID card, mentions a few 'families' who supposedly got jobs through him, and says the seats will fill up if you don't pay this week.

choices.text: Tell him you won't pay anything until you see the official vacancy notification on the department's own recruitment portal (SSC, KPSC, RRB, etc.) and verify his identity through the department's listed helpline — not the number he gave you.
choices.feedback: Correct. Public-sector jobs in India are filled only through published notifications and competitive exams — there is no legal channel where a 'contact' sells a seat for cash. Verifying through the department's own public channels, not the broker's, is what actually exposes the fraud.

choices.text: Pay the processing fee in cash since he showed an ID card and other families say he got them jobs too.
choices.feedback: This is exactly the mechanism: fake ID cards and staged 'success stories' from earlier victims (or plants) exist purely to build trust before the payment. A real recruiter never needs an ID card to justify collecting cash — the ID and the testimonials are the con, not proof.

choices.text: Pay a smaller 'token advance' now to hold the spot, planning to verify everything before making the final payment.
choices.feedback: Any payment at all pulls you into the funnel — once you've paid something, scammers use your own advance as leverage to demand more 'processing' or 'verification' fees. The only safe move is zero payment before independent verification.

choices.text: Ask a relative to pay through their bank account instead of yours, to keep your own record clean if it turns out to be fake.
choices.feedback: This doesn't reduce the actual risk — the money is gone either way if it's a scam, and it can drag your relative into the same fraud case. The only real protection is not paying until the offer is independently verified.

takeaways: Government recruitment in India runs only through published notifications and competitive exams (SSC, UPSC, KPSC, IBPS, Railways RRB) — never through a private 'contact' asking for cash.
Verify anyone claiming to be a government official by calling the department's official helpline or checking its public staff directory, not the number they hand you.

If you've already paid, file a complaint immediately at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 (National Cyber Crime helpline) — impersonating a government official is a criminal offence regardless of the amount involved.

quiz.q: A Bengaluru man was duped of how much money after being promised a government job with no interview?
quiz.why: In a separate case the same week, a fake DRDO officer swindled a woman out of ₹2.3 lakh — both scams relied on impersonating access to official channels.

quiz.q: The Kengeri–Hejjala railway under-bridge opened today, ending how many months of commuter ordeal in West Bengaluru?
quiz.why: The under-bridge removes a long-standing bottleneck that forced commuters on that stretch into lengthy detours.

quiz.q: Iran's military said it attacked US bases in which three countries today, as West Asia tensions escalated?
quiz.why: The escalation came the same day an LPG tanker carrying 28 Indian crew was attacked in Iranian waters, though all aboard were reported safe.

quiz.q: What is the minimum age to contest a Lok Sabha election in India?
quiz.why: The minimum age is higher for the Rajya Sabha and state Legislative Councils, where candidates must be at least 30.

quiz.q: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within India by length?
quiz.why: The Godavari, at roughly half the Ganga's length, is often called the 'Dakshin Ganga' for its size and cultural importance in peninsular India.
